props.gloss_en: Ulla: the halakha follows R' Yehuda [on muktze]
Shmuel: the halakha follows R' Shimon [on muktze]
the ships' mats: Rav forbade [moving them]
and Shmuel permitted
Levi, when they brought a [doubtful] tereifa before him on a Festival, would examine it only when sitting by a refuse heap
for he said: perhaps it will not be found kosher, and it is not fit even for dogs
the mishna: an animal that died -- one may not move it from its place
Ze'eiri explained it: of a consecrated animal; but of a non-sacred one, it is well
and R' Yochanan too said: the halakha follows R' Shimon
R' Yochanan: the halakha follows an unattributed mishna
the mishna: one may not split wood from beams, nor from a beam that broke on the Festival
R' Yochanan: that one -- he teaches it as R' Yosei bar Yehuda
the mishna: one may start [a fire] with a pile of straw, but not with the wood in the storehouse
there [the mishna speaks of] cedar and fir beams
muktze for monetary loss -- even R' Shimon concedes [it is muktze]
the mishna: one does not water or slaughter the desert animals, but one does water and slaughter the domestic ones
Beit Shammai: one lifts bones and peels off the table
Beit Hillel: one removes the whole board and shakes it
Rav Nachman: we have only [this]: Beit Shammai are like R' Yehuda
...and Beit Hillel like R' Shimon
throughout [the laws of] Shabbat the halakha follows R' Shimon
except muktze for repulsiveness -- and what is it? an old lamp [there the halakha is not like R' Shimon]
in muktze for repulsiveness too the halakha follows R' Shimon
except muktze for prohibition -- and what is it? a lamp that was lit on that Shabbat
the mishna: all vessels may be moved on Shabbat except the large saw and the plough-blade
